question: Which Linux companion app path should become canonical now that Windows Hub has shipped: the GTK/C PR, the Rust/GTK4 alternative, or a narrower maintainer-owned design first?
rationale: The issue is no longer a simple missing-Windows-and-Linux tracker; Windows is shipped, Linux has multiple large app proposals, and choosing the app architecture/security boundary is a maintainer product decision.

options.title: Choose a Linux PR track
options.body: Review the two open Linux companion PRs, pick one canonical implementation path, and ask the other to close, merge in ideas, or become a community experiment.

options.title: Split Linux-only tracker
options.body: Create or designate a narrower Linux companion issue and close this umbrella only after preserving Windows-shipped evidence and links to active Linux work.

options.title: Pause app intake
options.body: Leave this issue open as roadmap-only and pause large companion app PRs until maintainers write a smaller acceptance plan.

recommendation.title: Choose a Linux PR track
recommendation.body: Review the two open Linux companion PRs, pick one canonical implementation path, and ask the other to close, merge in ideas, or become a community experiment.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored the tracker, gave the GTK-native Linux direction in discussion, and is the strongest documented product-routing owner.
